JordanGrayson Allen scored a career-high 42 points on 11/10 vs. NOP and set the franchise record for three-pointers (10).Last Game RecapPHOENIX, ARIZONA – The Suns dropped their first Play-In Tournament game to the Trail Blazers (1-0) on April 14, falling 114-110. Despite Phoenix holding an 11-point (89-100) with 6:24 remaining in the contest, Portland closed the game on a 25-10 run. The Suns made just two field goals during the stretch and had four turnovers. Overall, the Trail Blazers shot 52.6% (10-of-19) from the floor while tallying 4 rebounds and 4 blocks in the fourth quarter. Portland knocked down 17 three-pointers to Phoenix’s 9. At halftime, the Trail Blazers had as many triples (12) as the Suns had 3FGA. Portland shot just 34.3% from deep in the regular season, the third worst mark in the NBA. Phoenix sat fifth in the league for threes per contest (14.8) while the Trail Blazers ranked seventh (14.1). Jalen Green posted 35 points, one shy of his 2025-26 season high, an addition to 5 rebounds. Green led all scorers with 22 points in the first half, his most in an opening half this season and tied for his most in any half in 2025-26. He shot a perfect 4-of-4 from the floor in the first quarter. Devin Booker tallied 22 points and 4 assists, while Dillon Brooks ended with 20 points, 7 rebounds, and 4 steals. Jordan Goodwin recorded 12 points (3-of-6 3FG) and 1 steal, and Royce O’Neale posted 7 points, 8 rebounds, and 4 steals.Play-In: The top six teams in each conference, ranked in order by win-loss records, qualify for the playoffs. – The Suns (0-1) fell to the Thunder (1-0) in their first game of the NBA Playoffs following a 119-84 loss on April 19. After Phoenix jumped out on a quick 5-0 run to begin the game, Oklahoma City responded with a 28-12 run to take an 11-point, 28-17, lead with 2:06 remaining in the first quarter. The Thunder lead remaining in double digits the rest of the way, extending up to as many as 39. OKC show 45.2% from the field to Phoenix’s 34.9% mark and turned 19 Suns turnovers into 34 points on the other end, while the Suns scored just 2 points off of 8 Thunder turnovers. Oklahoma City grabbed 19 offensive rebounds, leading to 25 second chance points and missed just two free throws on the night, finishing 21-for-23 from the charity stripe. Devin Booker scored a team-high 23 points, to go along with 6 rebounds and 2 assists. Dillon Brooks added 18 points, 7 rebounds, and 2 assists, while Jalen Green tallied 17 points and 5 rebounds.
